extraction_scope: Worker-6 bounded final mechanism adjudication from Results text, methods, table locators, and OA package figures; molecular-dynamics/CD claims are kept separate from direct SEM morphology.

mechanism_claims.claim_text: SEM evidence supports surface protuberances/cracks and outer-layer disruption in S. aureus cells treated with Stigmurin, StigA25, and StigA31 at MIC-related concentrations; no lysis or pore formation is claimed as directly proven.
mechanism_claims.entity_scope: Stigmurin, StigA25, and StigA31 against Staphylococcus aureus

source_locators.locator: xml:sec=11:2.9. Mechanism Associated with the Antimicrobial Effect of Peptides in S. aureus

mechanism_claims.limitations: SEM morphology supports outer-layer disruption but does not identify a single molecular binding target or prove pore formation.

mechanism_claims.claim_text: Molecular-dynamics simulations support stronger peptide interaction/contact with an anionic bacterial-membrane mimic for StigA25/StigA31, especially StigA31, but this remains computational mechanism context.
mechanism_claims.entity_scope: Stigmurin, StigA25, and StigA31 with POPG/POPE bacterial-membrane mimic
mechanism_claims.limitations: Computational interaction energy and distance profiles are not direct biochemical binding assays.

mechanism_claims.claim_text: Circular-dichroism and in silico structural evidence support environment-dependent alpha-helical/amphipathic structure for the peptides; this is structural support for membrane interaction, not a standalone killing mechanism.
mechanism_claims.entity_scope: Stigmurin, StigA25, and StigA31 secondary structure

source_locators.locator: xml:sec=6:2.4. Structural Conformation by Circular Dichroism (CD)

mechanism_claims.limitations: Structural conformation supports plausibility only and is not direct antimicrobial-mechanism proof.
